attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post, reproducing his own X thread.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'principled', 'thus far' and the scope (problems in the thread). It is a firm present-state observation.

contract.note: The plain reading (no demonstrated, systematic solution with reliable performance across the problem class; mitigations don't count) is an ordinary reading. 'Principled' has no threshold Marcus supplied, so the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: A January 2024 survey of 32+ ways to mitigate hallucination, which also lists their limitations. It shows mitigation, not a demonstrated complete solution, so it neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

Nature, October 2023: meta-learning gives systematic generalization on restricted benchmarks. It predates the target period and is narrow in scope, so it is background, not a solution to distribution shift in current LLMs.

reviews.rationale: The support condition needs a fairly complete record that every problem in the thread remained unsolved. The packet covers only hallucination and systematic generalization, and both items are context: they show progress, not principled solutions. Nothing in the packet meets the contradiction condition either. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own claim about what other figures said, written in his own post.

semantics.note: The firm claim is that leading figures acknowledged this. The 'may' belongs to the view being attributed, not to Marcus's assertion, so the hedge rule does not block scoring. The 2022 part is preserved.

contract.note: Reading 'many leading figures' as several prominent figures, not a consensus, is ordinary and fair. 'Pure LLM scaling' read as pretraining scale alone is reasonable. The vague 'many' leaves room for interpretation.

evidence.note: TIME, November 2024: Sutskever says gains from bigger models have plateaued. This predates the post.
NYT via Indian Express, December 2024: Hassabis says scaling no longer gives the same progress. His qualification is preserved.
Semafor, December 2024: Pichai says progress needs breakthroughs, not scaling alone. This is a weaker acknowledgment, and he is optimistic overall.
Nautilus, March 2022: Marcus warns of possible diminishing returns from scaling. This establishes only that he made the warning in 2022, not that it was correct.
Same NYT report: Altman, Amodei and Huang remain bullish. This rules out a consensus reading but does not negate the acknowledgments cited.

reviews.rationale: Dated reports from before January 6, 2025 show Sutskever, Hassabis and, more weakly, Pichai acknowledging limits to scaling alone. The same NYT report describes this view as widespread among the people it interviewed. A 2022 record confirms Marcus made a similar warning. Some leaders disagreed, but that does not undercut the claim's actual scope.
